# Flow Chemistry Design Brief: Photocatalyst-Free Aerobic Dehydrogenation of 6-Methyl-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroquinoline

---

## (1) Proposed Flow Setup

**Reaction:** Metal-free aerobic photodehydrogenation of 6-methyl-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroquinoline → 6-methylquinoline in DMSO, using O₂ as the terminal oxidant and 448 nm blue light as the sole energy input. No photocatalyst.

### Hardware

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Reactor type | FEP coil, 1.0 mm ID |
| Reactor volume | 124.2 mL |
| Light source | Manual strip LED, 448 nm, 62 mW/cm² (360° coil irradiation) |
| Temperature | 40.0 °C (passively reached via LED heating — no external heating required) |
| BPR | 3.9 bar |

### Feed Streams

**Stream A — Liquid (HPLC or syringe pump)**
- 6-methyl-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroquinoline, 0.5 M in DMSO
- Flow rate: 0.1875 mL/min

**Stream B — Gas (MFC)**
- Pure O₂
- 4.2024 sccm (STP) = 2.0 equiv relative to substrate at inlet/STP basis

Streams A and B are combined at a **T-mixer** upstream of the photoreactor to generate segmented Taylor (slug) flow before entering the irradiated coil region.

### Residence Times

- **Inlet/STP apparent residence time: 28.3 min** — this is the primary design and calibration basis, consistent with how KRICT experimental data are reported (O₂ equivalents controlled by MFC at STP)
- **In-channel residence time: 88.5 min** — actual time fluid spends inside the pressurised coil at 3.9 bar, 40 °C (gas compressed, volumetric flow reduced ~3×)

### Steady-State Protocol

Allow **≥3 residence times (~85 min liquid-equivalent)** before collecting product fractions. Collect ~0.5–1 mL fractions for yield analysis by HPLC or NMR.

---

## (2) Why These Conditions Were Chosen

### Wavelength and Light Source (448 nm)

The batch protocol specifies 450 ± 15 nm blue LEDs for direct photoexcitation of the substrate (or a substrate–DMSO EDA complex), followed by SET to dissolved O₂. The 448 nm strip LED is within this window and matches the available inventory used in the prior best-result experiment (KRICT 3-1, 51% yield). Note: the input value of "wavelength = 15 nm" in the raw protocol is a data entry error; the text unambiguously states 450 ± 15 nm.

The closest literature analogy supporting this hardware geometry is a published FEP coil photoreactor operated at 450 nm with a 10 mL coil at 0.1 mL/min and ~100 min residence time (Ir-photocatalysed coupling, single-phase liquid). While the mechanism differs (Ir photoredox vs. metal-free EDA/SET), the coil geometry and wavelength match directly support using an FEP coil at 448 nm as the appropriate hardware platform. A second analogy (aerobic photooxidation with O₂ gas, BPR, PFA tubing) supports the gas–liquid slug flow configuration and mandatory BPR use.

### Temperature (40.0 °C)

All four KRICT flow experiments showing measurable yield were conducted at 40 °C. This is a hard constraint for single-factor screening — only residence time is varied here. LED heating passively brings the coil to 40 °C without external temperature control, consistent with all prior measurements.

### Concentration (0.5 M in DMSO)

Matches the batch protocol and all KRICT entries. DMSO is not interchangeable — it appears to function both as solvent and potential EDA relay partner. Inner-filter analysis at 0.5 M in 1.0 mm ID FEP gives A ≈ 0.05 (Beer-Lambert, ε ≈ 1 M⁻¹cm⁻¹ at 448 nm for this substrate class), indicating acceptable photon penetration throughout the 1 mm path length.

### O₂ Delivery (2.0 equiv, MFC at 4.2024 sccm)

Matches KRICT 3-1 conditions. O₂ is a co-substrate, not an impurity to exclude. Deoxygenation of the feed would kill the reaction. The MFC delivers a defined stoichiometric ratio at STP; the in-channel O₂ concentration is maintained by the 3.9 bar BPR (Henry's law: dissolved O₂ ≈ 24.8 mM at these conditions). Gas–liquid interfacial area in Taylor flow provides a kLa of ~0.32 s⁻¹, giving O₂ transfer capacity ~42× the O₂ demand — mass transfer is not limiting.

### BPR (3.9 bar)

Required to: (i) maintain dissolved O₂ via Henry's law, (ii) sustain stable Taylor slug flow against uncontrolled degassing, and (iii) prevent solvent vaporisation (DMSO bp = 189 °C, so boiling is not a concern, but BPR is mandatory for gas–liquid systems). The 3.9 bar value is consistent with the KRICT 3-1 best result (3 bar used there); this design targets 3.9 bar as the set point.

### FEP Tubing, 1.0 mm ID

FEP is transparent to 448 nm (confirmed). The 1.0 mm ID reduces optical path length relative to the batch tube diameter (~13 mm), directly addressing the batch limitation of poor photon penetration. Material compatibility with DMSO at 40

pre_council_proposal.chemistry_notes: Single-factor residence-time refinement on the 20 mL Manual Setup coil using the same T=40°C, c=0.50 M, BPR=3 bar conditions proven in KRICT 3-1 (51% yield at t_inlet=68.9 min). Liquid flow reduced from 0.01123 to 0.010 mL/min (manual syringe pump minimum), increasing t_inlet from 68.9 to ~85.5 min — the maximum achievable on this setup. O2 held at exactly 2.0 equiv (inlet/STP). Mechanism requires blue light (448-450 nm) for direct substrate/EDA complex photoexcitation followed by SET to O2; DMSO is essential solvent and possible EDA relay. FEP tubing transparent to 448 nm. Slug flow at 3 bar provides high gas-liquid interfacial area (kLa enhancement vs batch). Batch limitations — poor photon penetration through 13 mm tube diameter and poor O2 mass transfer with balloon saturation — both addressed: 1 mm FEP ID gives ~4 mm path length vs 13 mm batch; segmented flow vs stagnant balloon-saturated solution. Analogy 3 (FEP coil, 450 nm, 100 min residence time, 0.1 mL/min, 10 mL) is most chemically relevant — same wavelength and coil geometry; adjusted to 20 mL coil and lower flow rate to match KRICT evidence base. No overreaction observed in measured data, so longer residence time is the primary lever.
